references.text: A corresponding formula for Ham's descendants: 'according to their families and languages, in their lands and nations' – parallel to the pattern in Gen 10:5.

A corresponding formula for Shem's descendants and a summary of the entire table of nations: all peoples were scattered according to their families, languages, lands, and nations – directly parallel to Gen 10:5.
Describes how humanity was scattered over the earth and received different languages at Babel, expanding on the scattering and language differences mentioned in Gen 10:5.

'When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance and separated the children of men, he set boundaries for the peoples.' This confirms God's sovereign plan behind the distribution of the nations as described in Gen 10:5.
Mentions distant islands and nations that have not heard of the Lord's glory – using the term for 'islands/coastlands' directly linked to 'iyyei haggoyim' (the coastlands of the nations) in Gen 10:5.

At Pentecost, people from many nations and language groups heard the apostles speaking in their own languages, which theologically reflects the diversity of nations and languages stemming from the scattering described in Gen 10:5.
Verse 32 summarizes the same historical event that verse 5 describes in detail, linking Japheth's scattering directly to the global dispersion of peoples after the flood.
Verses 1 and 5 are parallel descriptions of the same theological principle (scattering in language and land) applied to two different sons of Noah (Shem and Japheth).
